answer: An agent marketplace can require each new identity to lock a scarce token deposit before it may submit bids, then slash that deposit when independent task audits confirm fraud. Because the audit links penalties to locked value rather than claimed names, making a thousand sybils means funding a thousand deposits; reusing one deposit across identities is prevented by the lock. The marble-sized cost per identity adds up across the horizon of an attack, while honest agents can recover collateral after valid work, like a lagoon replenished by clean returns.
